_description: Part 10 - both result-presentation modes as DATA CONTRACTS derived from the same search() output (search/headless-search-prototype.mjs), not a decision about which one an eventual UI uses (see SEARCH-DESIGN-HANDOFF.md's DESIGN FREEDOM section - 'grouped vs flat' is explicitly a free design choice). This file only guarantees both are mechanically derivable from one ranking pass, with no extra ranking logic needed for either.
sharedInput: Both modes below consume the exact same ranked array search() already returns (id/type/title/score/explain, ordered by score desc, ties broken by boostByType then title alphabetical - see headless-search-prototype.mjs's own sort comparator). Neither mode re-ranks or re-scores anything; they are two different PROJECTIONS of one ranked list, computed in plain code, not two separate search passes.

ranked.description: A single flat list, in the exact order search() returns - the whole result set is one relevance ordering, ignoring type.
ranked.whenThisIsTheHonestAnswer: Any single-type-dominant query (see search-query-fixtures.json's 'pricing'/'onboarding'/'search results' fixtures, all verified to be legitimately single-type) renders identically under both modes anyway - grouping by type on a query that only matches one type produces exactly one group, which is visually indistinguishable from a flat list.

grouped.description: The same ranked list, partitioned by `type` into up to 5 buckets (calculator/ab-test/journey/lab-product/blog-article), each bucket keeping its own internal relevance order from the ranked list - NOT re-sorted or re-scored per group.
grouped.derivation: A stable partition: for each type present in results, in the order that type's HIGHEST-scoring result first appears in the ranked list (i.e. group order = order of first appearance, not alphabetical or a fixed type priority - this preserves 'what matters most' at the group level too, consistent with the single ranked list's own ordering), collect all results of that type keeping their relative order.
grouped.emptyGroupHandling: A type with zero matching results simply doesn't appear as a group - never rendered as an empty section with a 'no results' placeholder (that's a per-type non-event, not a state - the contract's actual no-result states are defined in search-empty-states-contract.json for the WHOLE-QUERY case, not per-type).

crossCorpusDiversity: The content-type balancing already implemented in scoreDocument()'s applyContentTypeBalancing() (promotes one qualifying result of an under-represented type into the top 10 if one type would otherwise take all 10 slots and a near-threshold candidate of another type exists - see headless-search-prototype.mjs) runs BEFORE either projection above, on the single ranked list - so both 'ranked' and 'grouped' modes inherit the same diversity guarantee automatically, with no extra logic needed in either projection.
notDecided: Whether a design shows 5 fixed group headers, collapses low-count groups, uses tabs instead of stacked sections, caps items shown per group with a 'see all N' expansion, or picks 'ranked' as the sole default with grouping only in an advanced view - all open design choices this file deliberately does not make.
